vocab.example: The main thing I want to improve on is speaking in large meetings.

listening.title: Interview question: your strengths and weaknesses

lines.speaker: Trang (HR Manager)
lines.text: Nam, could you tell me about your main strength at work?

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: I think I am adaptable. I joined a new team last year and worked well after two weeks.

lines.speaker: Trang (HR Manager)
lines.text: Can you give me a short example of that situation?

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: My company changed the whole process in March, and I helped two colleagues learn it quickly.

lines.speaker: Trang (HR Manager)
lines.text: Thank you. And what about a weakness you are working on?

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: The honest answer is that I used to overcommit and accept too many tasks.

lines.speaker: Trang (HR Manager)
lines.text: How do you handle that problem now?

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: My mentor taught me to check my workload first, so now I say no politely when I am full.

lines.speaker: Trang (HR Manager)
lines.text: Is there anything else you want to improve on this year?

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: Yes. My growth area is presenting in English, so I write a short self-assessment every month.

lines.speaker: Trang (HR Manager)
lines.text: That is a clear plan, and it also shows confidence in your own development.

questions.q: What does Nam say is his main strength?
What weakness does Nam talk about?
How does Nam follow his own progress?
options: He asks his manager every week

shadowing: My main strength is that I adapt quickly when the team changes its process.
The honest answer is that I used to accept too many tasks at once.
